div.head: Rect 7
div.ab: [7] Be æhteswane. Æhteswane, ðe ínhe[or]de healt, gebyreð stifearh ⁊ his gewirce, ðonne he s[p]ic behworfen hæfð, ⁊ elles ða gerihtu, ðe ðeowan men to gebyriað.

Æhtesƿane (id est seruo porcario), qui dominicum gregem curie custodit, pertinet habere stiferh (id est porcellum de sude) et suum geƿirce, quando bacones suos bene corrediauerit, et amplius eas rectitudines, que seruo iure pertinent.
Be æhTESWANE . Æhteswane ðe inherode healt gebyreð stifearh . 7 his gewirce ðonne he swic behworfen hæfð. 7 elles ða gerihtu ðe ðeowan men to gebyriað.
Be æhteswane Æhteswane ðe inheorde healt gebyreð stifearh and his gewirce, ðonne he spic behworfen hæfð, and elles ða gerihtu ðe ðeowan men to gebyriað.

Vom leibeigenen Schweinehirten. Dem hörigen Schweinehirten, welcher die Herde der Domäne hütet, gebührt ein Stallferkel und sein Geschlinge, sobald er Speck [und Schinken] zugerichtet hat, und sonst die Gerechtsame, die einem unfreien Manne gebühren.

Of the slave swineherd. To the unfree swineherd who keeps the herd of the demesne [for the lord] is due a sty-pig and his offal, once he has prepared the bacon [and hams, from the pigs slaughtered from the demesne herd not let out to rent], and otherwise the dues which belong to an unfree man.

Concerning the bound swineherd To the bound swineherd who holds the lord’s herd is due a little pig, and his perquisites when he has prepared the bacon, and all the other rights which pertain to bound men.

Enslaved Swineherd To the enslaved swineherd who oversees the estate’s herd is due a young pig, and his privileges when he has prepared the bacon, as well as all the other rights which pertain to an enslaved person.
div.note: B reads ‘inherode’ and ‘spic’; Liebermann prints ‘inhe[or]de’ and ‘s[p]ic’. The Quadripartitus's ‘hams’ is probably too narrow. Liebermann compares 6.2.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl unfrei 1c. 14a. Wærlaf wæs riht æht to einem Landgut, heold þa grægan swyn; Urk. XI. Jhs. Earle Landchar. 276.—Hirten herrschaftlicher Herde heissen auch auf Gütern 12. 13. Jhs. nach ihrem Vieh; Vinogradoff Vill. 319

Cf. Gl unfrei 1c. 14a. Wærlaf wæs riht æht to an estate, heold þa grægan swyn; charter of the 11th cent., Earle Landchar. 276.—On estates of the 12th and 13th cents., too, herdsmen of the lord's herds are named after their livestock; Vinogradoff Vill. 319

Wie inland zu gafolland, so bildet inheord Ggs. zur bäuerlichen Dorfherde. Vielleicht will Verf. nicht sagen, jedes Gut habe einen inswan (o. 4, 2c) neben diesem Leibeigenen; manches mochte nur diesen oder jenen halten; vielleicht identifiziert Verf. beide.—Der Relativsatz war nötig, weil wohl auch das Dorf und mancher Bauer leibeigene Hirten hielt

As inland stands to gafolland, so inheord forms the contrast to the peasants' village herd. Perhaps the author does not mean to say that every estate had an inswan (above 4, 2c) alongside this serf; many a one may have kept only the one or the other; perhaps the author identifies the two.—The relative clause was necessary because the village, and many a peasant, probably also kept serf herdsmen

Auch der Unfreie geniesst gerihtu, landside (8), freilich vielleicht nur Nahrung, Kleidung, Hausung als des Herrn Verpflichtung; die Last, die ihm die Herrschaft aufbürdet, wird nicht, wie beim Bauern, beschränkt; vgl. Maitland Domesday 328

The unfree man too enjoys gerihtu, landside (8), though perhaps only food, clothing and housing as the lord's obligation; the burden that the lordship lays on him is not limited, as it is for the peasant; cf. Maitland Domesday 328

Nicht ‘Schlachtschwein’ (Leo); vgl. swin stigian Ger 11. Die Glieder des Kompositums belegt Toller auch sonst. Auch der Schweinehirt von Glastonbury erhält jährlich ein Spanferkel; Vinogradoff Vill. 321. Vgl u. 15. Q braucht einen Ausdruck der Lex Salica; soue frz.: Schweinestall

Not ‘pig for slaughter’ (Leo); cf. swin stigian Ger 11. Toller attests the elements of the compound elsewhere too. The swineherd of Glastonbury likewise receives a sucking-pig every year; Vinogradoff Vill. 321. Cf. below 15. Q uses an expression of the Lex Salica; soue French: pigsty
